newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First supporters favour deal with Labour - poll.
newsitem.headline: NZ First supporters favour deal with Labour - poll.

text.p: New Zealand First supporters overwhelmingly favour a coalition deal with the main opposition Labour Party over the conservative ruling National Party according to a poll released on Friday.
The National Business Review-Consultus poll undertaken by UMR Insight showed that 45 percent of the 750 respondents favoured a deal with Labour against 37 percent who preferred National.
Of the 74 respondents identified as New Zealand First supporters 62 percent opted for Labour against 22 percent for National. Seven percent said neither.
Economic nationalist New Zealand First holds the balance of power between Labour and National after New Zealand's first election under a new proportional representation system on October 12.

Respondents to the poll were asked to choose between a National and New Zealand First coalition supported by free- market Act New Zealand, which holds eight seats, or a Labour-New Zealand First coalition with support from the Alliance, which holds 13.
The margin of error was 3.5 percent for the full survey and at its worst 11.4 percent for the sample of New Zealand First voters, a UMR Insight spokeswoman said.
Of the respondents identified as Alliance voters, 85 percent wanted New Zealand First to back Labour, while 83 percent of Labour supporters wanted New Zealand First to do a deal with their party.
Seventy-eight percent of National supporters wanted New Zealand First to opt for National, four percent for Labour and nine percent said neither.
The poll was taken between October 18 and October 20, before the parties began negotiations over who should form a government. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
